title: Signal satellite architecture and dashboard federation notes
content:
Purpose

Quick notes on an experiment for decentralizing signal ownership via a 'satellite' architecture and what dashboard federation looks like in practice. This doc captures the architecture sketch, concrete metric/tracing naming, a proposed dashboard sync pattern, and operational guardrails. Meant as a working document for the Satellite Signals sprint.

Context and motivation

- Problem: central observability has become a bottleneck for fast feature teams. Dashboards grow large, query costs spike, and owners are unclear. We want a model where small teams can run local "satellite" signal collections and dashboards while keeping provenance and global SLO alignment.
- Goals: reduce query cost, make dashboard ownership explicit, enable fast iteration for product teams, retain the ability to roll up signals for incidents and executive metrics.

High-level satellite model

- Satellite: small instrumentation + dashboards owned by a feature/team. Collects a compact set of signals (<= 12 tiles) relevant for the feature.
- Anchor: a global canonical metric for each class (latency, error-rate, cost, kv-warmth) that satellites map back to using mapping metadata.
- Federation layer: lightweight manifest published to central index (manifest includes owner, signal ids, sampling rates, queryable dataset pointers). The manifest is the only required cross-team contract.

Manifest (minimum fields)

- satellite_id: short id (team-feature)
- owner: (name + slack)
- canonical_mappings: list of canonical_metric -> local_metric mapping (see examples below)
- sample_budget: quota (traces/second)
- dashboard_manifest_url: confluence or repo link
- last_sync: YYYY-MM-DD

Metric provenance and naming conventions

Principles:
- Local metrics should be descriptive and start with team prefix: <team>.<feature>.<metric>
- Canonical metrics live under canonical.<class>.<metric> (e.g., canonical.latency.first_token_ms)
- Every metric must include a provenance tag: origin=satellite_id and instrument_version

Example metrics (satellite -> canonical mapping):
- ml-rewrite.prefetch-sat.prefetch_kv_hit_rate -> canonical.cache.kv_hit_rate
- ml-rewrite.prefetch-sat.first_token_p50_ms -> canonical.latency.first_token_ms (p50 semantics declared)
- suggestions.rich-editor.safety-review-failure_rate -> canonical.quality.output-hallucination_rate

Definitions to publish in the manifest (examples):
- canonical.latency.first_token_ms: time from request_received to first_token_emitted, measured in ms; histogram aggregatable; p50/p95/p99 derivations described in panel metadata.
- canonical.cache.kv_hit_rate: fraction of requests where kprefetch hit occurred in local kvcache; computed per request, averaged across 1m windows.

Tracing guidance for satellites

Span model notes:
- Span roots should still be created at edge proxies (to preserve end-to-end latency). Satellite instrumentation should attach child spans with tag satellite_id and signal_hint.
- Naming: <satellite_id>.<operation>.<phase> e.g., ml-rewrite-prefetch.SATELLITE_PREFETCH.kv_lookup
- Key tags (string): satellite_id, trace_origin (edge|satellite), request_tier (hosted|dedicated|private), tenant_id (if available), experiment_flag
- Correlation IDs: continue to use global_request_id; if satellite needs to create subrequests, create satellite_sub_id and log both ids.

Sampling policies

- Default: satellites should use adaptive sampling to keep trace budget under manifest.sample_budget. Use severity-weighted retention: keep all traces that triggered errors or regression signals, sample successful traces at 0.5%–2% depending on QPS.
- Hot-path captures: if span latency > p95 of canonical.latency.first_token_ms, override sampling to 100% for that request and mark sample_reason=latency_outlier.

Dashboard federation pattern

- Satellites host compact dashboards (microdash) in a per-team Grafana folder or an embedded observer UI. Panels are restricted to <= 12 visible tiles; each panel must declare: metric_id, canonical_mapping (if any), recommended refresh interval, and query_cost_estimate.
- A nightly sync job validates manifests and produces a central index page (read-only) that lists all satellites and links to their dashboards. The central index supports roll-up queries but should not attempt to render all satellite tiles live.

Panel metadata template (human-readable):
- title: string
- metric_id: <team>.<feature>.<metric>
- canonical_map: optional canonical.<class>.<metric>
- description: 1–2 lines with units and aggregation window
- owner: name
- cost_score: low|medium|high (estimated query cost)
- retention_notes: sampling policy or TTL

Roll-up and incident flows

- Incident play: on pager hit, responders can request a "roll-up snapshot" from the federation job which executes pre-authorized queries against satellite dashboards (bounded windows) and returns compressed series/CSV. This avoids ad-hoc heavy queries across many teams.
- SLO alignment: teams must map at least one local signal to the canonical latency or error rate for the service. If not mapped, central SRE will assign a default mapping and notify the owner.

Dashboard guardrails and cost controls

- Query budget: satellites must declare a monthly query budget in manifest. Exceeding budgets triggers auto-throttling for non-critical panels (experimental).
- Panel review: any panel with cost_score=high needs a 1:1 with Observability team and must include preview of query and sample cardinality estimates.

Operational runbook snippets

- On high-cost alert from index: run federation-rollup --window=10m --limit=20 --teams=(top-10-cost)
- On missing canonical mapping: contact owner via manifest.owner slack, create a ticket JIRA-INF-xxxx mapping assignment.

Open questions / TODOs

- Backwards compatibility: how to ingest older satellites that do not publish manifests? (proposal: a registrar tool that scans folders monthly and prompts owners)
- How strict should canonical semantics be? e.g., different teams compute kv_hit_rate subtly differently. We need canonical tests (unit test snippets) that teams can run locally to validate mapping.
- Panel cost estimation methodology: we need a small tool to run dry-run queries on sample data and return cost_score.

Action items (first pass)

- Aisha: prototype manifest schema + registrar script (due 2025-08-01)
- Ben: sample satellite Grafana folder template + microdash layout (due 2025-08-08)
- Carlos: roll-up snapshot job prototype (due 2025-08-15)
- Run a pilot with 3 teams (ml-rewrite, embeddings-serving, console-rollouts) in Q3 2025.

Notes to reviewers

- This is intentionally lightweight and experimental. Looking for feedback on the manifest fields and the sampling defaults. Prefer practical guardrails over heavy governance.

Recent edits:
- 2026-01-12: clarified tracing span naming and added sample_budget field to manifest (Aisha)
- 2025-11-02: added operational runbook snippets and cost control section (Ben)
